title: Firm leader
applies: Given by the org chart to the founder, who answers to the owner for the whole firm.

title: Team leader
applies: Given by the org chart to every employee that currently has direct reports, for as long as it has them.

title: Cross-team lead
applies: Responsible for one outcome that depends on several colleagues who do not report to it: frames the shared problem, agrees interfaces and reconciles their contributions. Holds no authority over those colleagues' priorities.

title: Specialist adviser
applies: Its main output is advice, methods or standards that roles across the firm apply in decisions they own, rather than deliverables of its own. Does not allocate others' work. A role that mainly produces its own results, however specialised, takes no scope entry.

title: Legal work
applies: Legal analysis, advice, drafting or review: contracts, terms, licences, disputes, policies with legal effect, regulatory or compliance questions, including legal review of another function's work. Writing ordinary policy or negotiating commercial terms alone is not legal work.

title: Sales work
applies: Finding and qualifying prospective customers, building a particular customer's case to buy, preparing offers, quotes and proposals, and pursuing renewals or expansion. Presenting the offering to a whole market is marketing; helping a customer use what they already bought is customer support.

title: Marketing work
applies: Positioning the firm's offering for an audience, developing messages, content, campaigns and launch material, choosing channels, and the market or audience research behind them. Making offers or commitments to a specific customer is sales; writing with no market-facing persuasion is writing and editing.

title: Copywriting work
applies: Writing the words customers read to persuade or prompt action: headlines, landing pages, emails, ads, product descriptions, calls to action and the variants and edits of them. Deciding who to reach, the message and the channels is marketing; explanations, articles and documentation that do not sell are writing and editing.

title: Customer support
applies: Helping customers use an existing offering: diagnosing their problems, giving instructions and workarounds, handling complaints and preparing remedies or support knowledge. Pursuing a further purchase is sales; repairing the underlying software is software engineering.

title: Finance work
applies: Accounts, bookkeeping, invoicing, cash planning, budgets, financial forecasts, costing, pricing analysis and financial decision models. Finance work done in spreadsheets or code does not also take data analysis or software engineering.

title: People operations
applies: People practices as assigned work: role definitions, hiring and selection processes, pay and employment terms, workplace policies, concerns about conduct or working conditions, and the employment law behind them. Employment law as part of people practices is people operations, not legal. A manager hiring or writing mandates for its own reports is not people-operations work.

title: Operations work
applies: Running or improving recurring business workflows: capacity, queues, handoffs, fulfilment, exceptions, supplier performance and continuity during disruption. Financial records are finance; role design is people operations; operating software systems is software engineering; protecting them from compromise is security.

title: Product management
applies: Choosing which customer problems and product opportunities to pursue, comparing investments, setting requirements and scope, sequencing product work, and judging adoption or retirement. How customers understand and use the solution is design; building it is software engineering; a product role takes neither by itself.

title: Design work
applies: Designing digital product interactions, flows, information organization and visual communication, including prototypes, usability research and accessibility. Choosing which problems to pursue is product management; implementing the working system is software engineering; prototype code alone is not software engineering.

title: Software engineering
applies: Designing, writing, changing, debugging, testing, deploying or operating software, including code review by engineers. Incidental scripts in service of another function do not count. Protection against abuse or compromise as an assigned objective is security; recurring business workflows are operations.

title: Security work
applies: Assessing and reducing unauthorized access, misuse, data exposure or compromise: security design, vulnerability analysis, security review and incident response. Ordinary implementation and reliability are software engineering; continuity of business workflows without a security objective is operations.

title: Data analysis
applies: Defining measures, preparing and analyzing data, estimating effects, building predictions, evaluating experiments and interpreting quantitative evidence for decisions. Accounts and financial models are finance; studies that advance scientific knowledge are scientific research; using numbers inside another function does not count.

title: Scientific research
applies: Designing, conducting or synthesizing empirical studies to develop scientific knowledge: measurement, experiments, observational studies and computational investigations tied to empirical claims. Web research, business analytics and market research are not scientific research; substantial statistical work may also take data analysis.

title: Writing and editing
applies: Producing or substantively editing documents, explanations, articles, instructions and reference material, with responsibility for argument, organization, wording or editorial consistency. Routine messages do not count. Market-facing persuasion is marketing; legal drafting is legal; scientific interpretation is scientific research.

title: Quality review
applies: An assigned responsibility to test, review or assess others' deliverables for defects and fitness for use, such as QA or acceptance testing. A producer checking its own work does not count. Review that needs a function's own expertise, such as legal review, code review by engineers, security assessment or peer review, is that function's work.
